subproblem.title: Diagonal extraction from nested infinite index sets (Simon 7.2 proof, choice of the subsequence j_r)
subproblem.statement: Let Q(r, i, j) (r, i, j ∈ ℕ) be an arbitrary relation. Assume that for every r ∈ ℕ and every infinite set J ⊆ ℕ there is an infinite set J' ⊆ J such that Q(r, i, j) holds for all i, j ∈ J'. Then there is a strictly increasing map φ : ℕ → ℕ such that Q(r, φ(r), φ(r+1)) holds for every r ∈ ℕ.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (Q : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → Prop), (∀ r : ℕ, ∀ J : Set ℕ, J.Infinite → ∃ J' ⊆ J, J'.Infinite ∧ ∀ i ∈ J', ∀ j ∈ J', Q r i j) → ∃ φ : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono φ ∧ ∀ r : ℕ, Q r (φ r) (φ (r + 1))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 6, proof of 7.2: “apply (1) with ε = 1, 1/2, 1/4 etc. to extract a subsequence {T_{j_r}}_{r=1,2,…} from {T_j} such that d_W̃(T_{j_{r+1}}, T_{j_r}) < 2^{−r}”.

This is the combinatorial content of Steps 1–2 of the parent proof, abstracted to an arbitrary relation Q(r, i, j). In the parent, Q(r, i, j) says that T_i − T_j = ∂R + S with R, S integer multiplicity and M(R) + M(S) < 2^{−r}. No property of Q beyond the hypothesis is used.

1. (Choice function.) By the hypothesis and the axiom of choice, fix for every r ∈ ℕ and every infinite J ⊆ ℕ a set F(r, J) with:
   - F(r, J) ⊆ J;
   - F(r, J) is infinite;
   - Q(r, i, j) holds for all i, j ∈ F(r, J).
   (Lean: `choose F hFsub hFinf hFQ using h`, with F : (r : ℕ) → (J : Set ℕ) → J.Infinite → Set ℕ.)

2. (Nested infinite sets.) Define J_0 := ℕ and J_{r+1} := F(r, J_r).
   Simultaneously, by induction on r, every J_r is infinite: J_0 = ℕ is infinite, and if J_r is infinite then F(r, J_r) is defined and infinite by step 1. So the recursion is well defined.
   (Lean: a sequence in the subtype {J : Set ℕ // J.Infinite}, defined by `Nat.rec ⟨univ, infinite_univ⟩ (fun r J => ⟨F r J.1 J.2, hFinf r J.1 J.2⟩)`.)
   By step 1, for every r ∈ ℕ:
   (a) J_{r+1} ⊆ J_r;
   (b) Q(r, i, j) holds for all i, j ∈ J_{r+1}.

3. (Unboundedness.) If A ⊆ ℕ is infinite, then for every m ∈ ℕ there is x ∈ A with m < x. Otherwise A ⊆ {0, 1, …, m} would be finite. (Lean: `Set.Infinite.exists_gt`.)
   Apply this to the infinite sets J_{r+1}. Fix, for all r, m ∈ ℕ, an element g(r, m) ∈ J_{r+1} with m < g(r, m).

4. (Definition of φ.) Define recursively φ(0) := g(0, 0) and φ(r+1) := g(r+1, φ(r)).
   By step 3, φ(0) ∈ J_1 and φ(r+1) ∈ J_{r+2}; that is, φ(r) ∈ J_{r+1} for every r ∈ ℕ (case distinction r = 0 or r = s+1).
   Moreover φ(r) < g(r+1, φ(r)) = φ(r+1) for every r ∈ ℕ.

5. (Strict monotonicity.) Since φ(r) < φ(r+1) for every r, φ is strictly increasing. Indeed, for r < s, induction on s gives φ(r) < φ(s): if s = r + 1 this is step 4, and φ(r) < φ(s) implies φ(r) < φ(s) < φ(s+1). (Lean: `strictMono_nat_of_lt_succ`.)

6. (Consecutive pairs.) Fix r ∈ ℕ.
   - By step 4, φ(r) ∈ J_{r+1} and φ(r+1) ∈ J_{r+2}.
   - By step 2(a) applied at r + 1, J_{r+2} ⊆ J_{r+1}, so φ(r+1) ∈ J_{r+1}.
   - Hence both φ(r) and φ(r+1) lie in J_{r+1} = F(r, J_r), and step 2(b) gives Q(r, φ(r), φ(r+1)).

7. (Conclusion.) φ is strictly increasing by step 5, and Q(r, φ(r), φ(r+1)) holds for every r ∈ ℕ by step 6. ∎
proof_key_steps: Choose F(r, J) ⊆ J infinite such that Q(r, ·, ·) holds on all pairs from F(r, J).
Define the nested infinite sets J_0 = ℕ and J_{r+1} = F(r, J_r), so that J_{r+1} ⊆ J_r and Q(r, ·, ·) holds on J_{r+1}.
Recursively pick φ(0) ∈ J_1 and φ(r+1) ∈ J_{r+2} with φ(r+1) > φ(r), using Set.Infinite.exists_gt.
φ(r) and φ(r+1) both lie in J_{r+1}, hence Q(r, φ(r), φ(r+1)).

audit.reason: The prose and standalone one-line proposition agree, and fiw_fcl_nested_subseq is a bare, unreserved identifier. The supplied proof completely constructs nested infinite sets and increasing indices with φ(r) ∈ J_{r+1}. Nesting places both consecutive indices in J_{r+1}, establishing the ordered relation without assuming symmetry. The obligation is independent, non-circular and supplies precisely the parent's extraction step.

subproblem.title: Telescoping identification of the weak limit (Simon 7.2 proof: T − T_{j_ℓ} = ∂R^(ℓ) + S^(ℓ) from (5))
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (Tr : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn U n) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn U (n + 1)) (S : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn U n) (X : GeometricCurrentOn U (n + 1)) (Y : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ℓ : ℕ), (∀ r ω, Tr r ω - Tr (r + 1) ω = (R r).boundary ω + S r ω) → WeaklyConvergesOn Tr T → (∀ η, HasSum (fun k => R (ℓ + k) η) (X η)) → (∀ ω, HasSum (fun k => S (ℓ + k) ω) (Y ω)) → ∀ ω, Tr ℓ ω - T ω = X.boundary ω + Y ω
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 6, proof of 7.2, last paragraph: “by 3.13 we can define integer multiplicity R^(ℓ), S^(ℓ) by the M-absolutely convergent series R^(ℓ) = Σ_{r=ℓ}^∞ R_r, S^(ℓ) = Σ_{r=ℓ}^∞ S_r; … and (from (5)) T − T_{j_ℓ} = ∂R^(ℓ) + S^(ℓ)”.

This is Step 4 of the parent proof, isolated:
- T_r plays the role of T_{j_r};
- the increments are written in the order T_r − T_{r+1} = ∂R_r + S_r, so the conclusion reads T_ℓ − T = ∂X + Y with no sign change;
- X and Y play the roles of R^(ℓ) and S^(ℓ).
Only the pointwise series identities (c) and (d) are used; integrality and mass play no role.

1. (Boundary as evaluation at dω.) Fix ω ∈ D^n(U) and put dω := exteriorDerivativeTestOn U n ω ∈ D^{n+1}(U).
   By definition of the boundary, ∂Z(ω) = Z(dω) for every Z ∈ D_{n+1}(U) (`GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply`).
   Hence hypothesis (a) at r reads T_r(ω) − T_{r+1}(ω) = R_r(dω) + S_r(ω), and the goal is T_ℓ(ω) − T(ω) = X(dω) + Y(ω).

2. (Telescoping.) For every N ∈ ℕ,
   T_ℓ(ω) − T_{ℓ+N}(ω) = Σ_{k=0}^{N−1} (R_{ℓ+k}(dω) + S_{ℓ+k}(ω)).
   Induction on N. For N = 0 both sides are 0. If the identity holds for N, then
   T_ℓ(ω) − T_{ℓ+N+1}(ω) = (T_ℓ(ω) − T_{ℓ+N}(ω)) + (T_{ℓ+N}(ω) − T_{ℓ+N+1}(ω))
                         = Σ_{k=0}^{N−1} (R_{ℓ+k}(dω) + S_{ℓ+k}(ω)) + (R_{ℓ+N}(dω) + S_{ℓ+N}(ω)),
   by the induction hypothesis and step 1 with r = ℓ + N. This is the sum up to k = N.
   (Lean: `Finset.sum_range_succ`, rewrite with the induction hypothesis and (a), then `ring`.)

3. (Limit of the left side.) The map N ↦ ℓ + N tends to ∞, since ℓ + N ≥ N. (Lean: `tendsto_atTop_mono (fun N => Nat.le_add_left N ℓ) tendsto_id`.)
   So by hypothesis (b) at ω, T_{ℓ+N}(ω) → T(ω) as N → ∞.
   Hence T_ℓ(ω) − T_{ℓ+N}(ω) → T_ℓ(ω) − T(ω).

4. (Limit of the right side.) By (c) at η := dω and (d) at ω, the real series Σ_k R_{ℓ+k}(dω) and Σ_k S_{ℓ+k}(ω) have sums X(dω) and Y(ω).
   Hence Σ_k (R_{ℓ+k}(dω) + S_{ℓ+k}(ω)) has sum X(dω) + Y(ω) (`HasSum.add`).
   The partial sums Σ_{k=0}^{N−1} of a series over ℕ with a sum converge to that sum (`HasSum.tendsto_sum_nat`).
   So the right side of step 2 tends to X(dω) + Y(ω) as N → ∞.

5. (Uniqueness of limits.) By step 2, the sequences in steps 3 and 4 coincide for every N. Limits of a sequence in the Hausdorff space ℝ along atTop are unique (`tendsto_nhds_unique`).
   Therefore T_ℓ(ω) − T(ω) = X(dω) + Y(ω), which equals ∂X(ω) + Y(ω) by step 1.

6. (Conclusion.) Since ω ∈ D^n(U) was arbitrary, T_ℓ(ω) − T(ω) = ∂X(ω) + Y(ω) for all ω ∈ D^n(U). ∎
proof_key_steps: Rewrite ∂Z(ω) = Z(dω) with dω = exteriorDerivativeTestOn U n ω (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply).
Telescoping by induction on N: T_ℓ(ω) − T_{ℓ+N}(ω) = Σ_{k<N} (R_{ℓ+k}(dω) + S_{ℓ+k}(ω)).
The left side tends to T_ℓ(ω) − T(ω) by weak convergence along ℓ + N → ∞.
The right side tends to X(dω) + Y(ω) by HasSum.add and HasSum.tendsto_sum_nat.
Uniqueness of limits in ℝ gives T_ℓ(ω) − T(ω) = ∂X(ω) + Y(ω).

audit.reason: The prose includes every hypothesis of the standalone one-line proposition, and fiw_fcl_telescope_limit is a bare, unreserved identifier. Boundary evaluation is valid for arbitrary U. The supplied induction telescopes with the correct sign; weak convergence along ℓ+N and the two HasSum hypotheses give identical partial-sum sequences whose real limits are unique. No openness, integrality, mass assumption or parent conclusion is silently used. The complete proof requires no sibling dependency.
